column1: “My state still isn't paying the ₦70,000 minimum wage.”
column2: That's wrong, and you're right to be angry. President Tinubu signed the ₦70,000 minimum wage into law in July 2024, and it binds every employer, including state governments. States are also receiving much bigger allocations than before. Ask your governor why he isn't paying.
column3: National Minimum Wage Act signed 29 July 2024 (up from ₦30,000). The NLC ordered May Day 2026 protests in defaulting states.

column2: I agree it's not enough with today's prices. It was more than double the old ₦30,000, and it's a floor, not a ceiling. Labour has already started pushing for the next review, and that conversation will continue.
column3: Labour proposed ₦154,000 in March 2026. Don't promise a figure.

column1: Why can't the Federal Government simply force states to pay the minimum wage?
column2: Nigeria is a federation: states employ and pay their own workers from their own budgets. The FG set the legal floor and increased allocations; enforcement runs through labour action and the courts.
column3: Point voters to their governor, not Abuja, on unpaid state wages.
